messages:
kai: Heads up — seeing a sharp p95 token-latency spike on dedicated pool-storm since the 23:38 deploy. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/pool-storm -> p95 tokens +115%. KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~82% -> ~34% at same time. Kernel-select tweak was rolled at 23:38 from canary -> prod. Any quick theories? :thinking:

meera: Copying graphs here. Looks correlated to the kernel-select change and a small bump in average batch size. Also noticed route distribution shifted — /chat-heavy accounts for ~60% of requests in the window. Could be cache eviction behavior interacting with kernel selection heuristics.

perf-bot: ALERT: pool-storm p95_token_latency increased by 115% (baseline rolling 6h). KV_cache_hit_rate decreased by 48pp. Triggered at 2026-05-12T23:41:12Z.

liam: Can we confirm which kernel variant was chosen for long sequences? The new selector prefers kernel-v2 for small batches but may pick fallback for longer seqs. I can try quick revert if we think it's the cause.

meera: I pulled a few profiler samples during the spike — attaching condensed output: ```
# profiler snapshot (condensed)
hotspots:
 - attention_kernel_v2: 34% cpu, increased wall time vs baseline
 - kv_cache_lookup: latency doubled (median 1.8ms -> 3.9ms)
 - batching_coordinator: more flushes, avg batch size +0.7 tokens
call stacks show repeated cache misses leading to additional recompute of past KV segments.
```

natalie: Also see ~12% increase in prefill time in the traces for /chat-heavy. If kernel-v2 has different memory access patterns it could be causing more frequent eviction of small KV shards under current allocator thresholds.

kai: Good point. Meera — can you run the route-level kv hit query? If /chat-heavy has longer prefixes, that would explain miss rate.

meera: Running quick query now (samples): ```sql
SELECT route, count(*) as qps, approx_percentile(seq_len, 0.5) as med_seq
FROM request_metrics
WHERE pool = 'pool-storm' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY qps DESC
LIMIT 20;
-- results: /chat-heavy qps=320 med_seq=920, /short-reply qps=120 med_seq=48
```

liam: OK — rollout seems to have pushed kernel-v2 for mid-sized batches which are now getting long sequences and thrashing the KV cache. I'm going to roll the kernel-select flag back to baseline on pool-storm and watch. Will post command before running.

liam: Running: ```bash
kgctl deploy --pool pool-storm --set kernelselect.variant=baseline --image serving/runtime:2026-02-01 --strategy rolling --timeout 10m
```

perf-bot: DEPLOY: kernelselect rollback started by liam at 2026-05-12T23:48:05Z.

perf-bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS: rollback complete on pool-storm at 2026-05-12T23:50:12Z. Health checks OK.

kai: After rollback: p95 token latency trending back to baseline over last 2 minutes. KV cache hit-rate recovering (now ~78%). Looks like kernelselect was the main driver.

natalie: Filing follow-up: add per-route KV-hit and kernel-variant heatmap to the Dedicated Capacity dashboard + an alert when route-level KV hit drops >20pp in 5m. Also add a canary gating check for long-sequence routes before promoting kernelselect changes to prod.

meera: Agreed. Also want a short postmortem on why selector logic didn't account for median sequence length per route. I'll draft action items.

kai: Thanks all. Marking thread resolved for now. If we see recurrence reopen. :white_check_mark:
